request: Add cylindrical pin into the bearing area of the part, so it is able to rotate around it.

actions.relational_constraint: Position the pin into the bearing area so that the applicable component can rotate around the pin.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the bearing area, its rotational axis, the component intended to rotate, and the required pin diameter, length, position, and orientation from the CAD model.
steps: Localize the bearing area at the negative-x clevis end. The primary bearing geometry is the coaxial transverse bore formed by the positive-y clevis cheek S02 and negative-y clevis cheek S03. Use positive lug bore wall face 0006 (FACE 0) and negative lug bore wall face 0007 (FACE 1) as the principal cylindrical references.

Use the cylindrical axes extracted from faces 0006 and 0007 to define one common pin axis. The model description establishes that this axis is parallel to the global y direction and that both bore portions have a radius of 3 mm, giving a nominal existing bore diameter of 6 mm.

Use positive lug inner cheek face 0005 (FACE 4) at y=3.5 mm and negative lug inner cheek face 0008 (FACE 3) at y=-3.5 mm as secondary references. These faces identify the 7 mm-wide central clevis slot and verify that the pin must pass through both cheeks and across S04 without being fused to the slot or cheek geometry.

Create a new pin as a separate component or separate solid body rather than adding material to the lever. Do not merge the pin with S02, S03, or S04, because a Boolean union would prevent the required relative rotation.

Create a datum plane normal to the common bore axis, preferably coincident with one outer clevis side or offset from the longitudinal x-z center plane at y=0. Project the circular edge or axis of either bore portion into the sketch so the new pin is constrained concentric with faces 0006 and 0007.

Sketch a circle for the pin shaft. Set its nominal diameter from the 6 mm bore and apply the required rotational running clearance according to the manufacturing process and fit standard; the finished shaft must not exceed the effective bore diameter. If only nominal CAD geometry is required, use a 6 mm nominal shaft and represent the clearance through tolerances or assembly-fit metadata.

Extrude the circular profile along the y-axis through the positive-y cheek, the central S04 clevis clearance region, and the negative-y cheek. Define the pin length from the two outer clevis side extents, with only the intended end projection needed for assembly and retention. Confirm that the shaft continuously overlaps both cylindrical bearing walls 0006 and 0007.

Add small equal chamfers or rounded lead-ins to both circular pin ends to support insertion through the two bore portions and to avoid damaging the bore edges. Keep all chamfers outside the active cylindrical bearing length.

If axial retention is required, add a suitable head, retaining-ring groove, cross-hole, upset end, or other retention detail as a separate pin feature. Do not select a retention method until the allowable axial projection and assembly method are specified.

Insert or position the completed pin using a concentric constraint between the pin shaft and the common axis of faces 0006 and 0007. Add only the axial constraint required to prevent unintended translation; do not apply a rotational lock.

Define a revolute joint about the pin axis between the tapered clevis-to-hook lever and the fixed pin or its supporting assembly. The lever's rotation is supported by S02 and S03, while S04 remains open to receive a mating link and provides clearance around the middle portion of the pin.

Run an interference and clearance check across the full intended rotation. Verify shaft clearance against faces 0006 and 0007, axial clearance at the pin ends and outer cheek surfaces, and clearance within the clevis slot bounded by faces 0005 and 0008.

Leave the original lever sections unchanged unless the selected manufacturing fit requires explicit bore finishing, lead-in chamfers, or dimensional adjustment. No removal from S01 or S05 is required, and the hook geometry is unrelated to the rotational bearing interface.

intention: Enable the applicable part or component to rotate around the added pin.
